# Research summary: Solar-panel efficiencies (concise)

## Overview
This short research summary compiles documented ranges and recent records for photovoltaic (PV) efficiencies across major technologies, contrasts laboratory (record) vs real‑world (commercial/module/system) performance, summarizes the principal environmental and design factors that reduce output, and highlights recent trends and breakthrough areas. Sources include IEA‑PVPS and Fraunhofer reviews, NREL/Fraunhofer record charts, manufacturer datasheets and recent industry reporting.

## Typical efficiencies by major technologies (commercial/module level)
- Monocrystalline crystalline silicon (mono‑c-Si): commonly 20–24% module efficiency for mass‑market modules; premium commercial/residential modules (e.g., IBC/HJT/Maxeon-style) reach ~22–24% in production. Fraunhofer’s industry survey reports a weighted average for c‑Si wafer‑based modules near 22–23% in recent quarters. (See references.)
- Polycrystalline / multicrystalline c‑Si: historically 15–19% in mass production; largely displaced by mono in many markets but still present in budget/utility segments.
